turns.html: Sizing the sacrificial-anode CP for a fixed steel jacket — can you run it to DNV-RP-B401?

Happy to — a few details so I run it right:
  • Exposure zones and wetted areas — submerged, splash, atmospheric?
  • Coating category in each zone?
  • Design life, and the seawater temperature & resistivity?
  • Anode type and unit mass?
This runs the DNV-RP-B401 zone-by-zone screen — current demand per zone, anode mass from charge, then a current-output check on the anode count.

Fixed steel jacket — 5,000 m² submerged (coating cat I), 300 m² splash (cat III), 200 m² atmospheric (cat I). 25-year design life, seawater 10 °C, resistivity 0.30 Ω·m. Aluminium stand-off anodes, 200 kg each, utilisation 0.85. Make-up's in the file.

Got it — three exposure zones, so I'll run DNV-RP-B401 zone by zone. Basis I'll use: current demand per zone from area × density × coating breakdown (initial/final), total charge → anode mass, then a current-output check that the anode bank can actually deliver the final demand. Running it now…

Here's the design — and it flags the governing criterion:
QuantityResultCheckVerdict
Mean current demand101.9 Afinal 168.6 A—
Required anode mass13,121 kg——
Anodes by mass (200 kg)66——
Anodes by current output109governs✅ Use 109
Mass alone needs 66 stand-off anodes, but to push the 168.6 A final demand through the anode resistance you need 109 — so the current-output check governs. Deckhand flags the higher count so the jacket actually stays protected.

report.title: Jacket CP Design (DNV-RP-B401)
report.inputs:
Structure — exposure zones
Submerged 5,000 m² · coating cat I
Splash 300 m² · coating cat III
Atmospheric 200 m² · coating cat I

Design & environment
Design life 25 yr · seawater 10 °C · resistivity 0.30 Ω·m

Anodes
Al stand-off · 200 kg each · utilisation 0.85
capacity 2,000 Ah/kg · resistance 0.161 Ω
report.methodology:
1 · Current demand per zone = area × density × coating breakdown (mean & final).
2 · Coating breakdown — submerged 0.30/0.55 · splash 0.875/1.0 · atmospheric 0.30/0.55.
3 · Total charge over 25 yr (219,000 h) → anode mass (capacity 2,000 Ah/kg, utilisation 0.85).
4 · Anode count by mass, then by current output (Ohm's law through the anode resistance at final demand).
5 · The larger count governs.
report.outputs:
QuantityValueNote
Total wetted area5,500 m²3 zones
Demand — submerged75.0 / 137.5 Amean / final
Demand — splash26.3 / 30.0 Amean / final
Demand — atmospheric0.6 / 1.1 Amean / final
Total current demand101.9 / 168.6 Amean / final
Required anode mass13,120.7 kg66 × 200 kg
Anodes by current output1091.55 A each
Verdict: USE 109 ANODES — mass needs 66, but the current-output check (final demand 168.6 A vs 102.2 A from 66 anodes) governs at 109.
